programs.title: Molecules on the Spree: Atoms, Structures and Public AI
outcomes: Explain basic molecular structure using the Molecule Man sculpture as a life-size model
Describe how an agent-managed, human-governed DAO makes decisions
Compare how decisions are made by voting vs. delegation

sessions.activity: Guided walk-activity linking the 30-metre molecular figure to atoms and bonds; students map a simple DAO charter like a molecular structure.
Learners act as 'Evidence Monitors': summarize one short, age-appropriate article about the Spree River or molecular science into a three-sentence brief.
Teams draft a mock proposal to improve a neighborhood issue; agents (facilitators) draft, students debate and hold the final vote.
Students create a simple progress chart tracking their proposals against measurable outcomes, mirroring the Progress Tracker agent.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized quiz scores on molecular-structure and DAO-literacy questions; aggregate counts of proposal themes (no names, no free text with identifying details).
programs.consent: Written guardian/parent consent required before participation, plus student assent; no photos or personal data collected; all shared data aggregated and anonymized per school privacy policy and GDPR.

programs.title: Worker Voice in Agent-Managed Systems
outcomes: Explain how agent-run operations with human-reserved votes affects workers
Identify the five human-reserved governance actions
Practice drafting a workplace proposal through an agent-drafted pipeline

sessions.activity: Workshop mapping how the Task Router and working groups coordinate work; participants compare to shop-floor task allocation.
Participants draft a workplace-resolution; a facilitator models the Proposal & Grant Drafter role, then the group debates and votes as the human body.
Review the human-reserved actions list; small groups design a worker-protection clause for a mock charter amendment (not enacted).
Participants define measurable outcomes for their mock clause and set up a simple tracking sheet.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized pre/post survey results on AI-governance literacy; aggregated theme counts from mock proposals; no individual responses shared.
programs.consent: Participation voluntary and off-worktime or per works-council agreement; GDPR-compliant notice; individuals can opt out of data sharing without losing training access.

programs.title: Evidence-to-Proposal Lab for Civil Society Teams
outcomes: Run an evidence-monitoring workflow from source to summary
Convert synthesized evidence into a fundable proposal outline
Apply human-in-the-loop checks to AI-drafted documents

sessions.activity: Teams practice the Evidence Monitor and Research Synthesis Agent workflow: gather sources, summarize, and flag uncertainty in a one-page brief.
Teams turn their brief into a proposal outline using the drafter-agent pattern; peers review for claims that lack evidence before any human decision point.
Participants design a working-group structure and task-routing board for one of their own NGO projects.
Teams define 3 measurable outcomes for their proposal and build a simple progress-tracking dashboard.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized proposal outlines and evaluation rubric scores to a shared example library; aggregated workflow time data; organization names optional and revocable.
programs.consent: Organizational memorandum of consent plus individual opt-in; GDPR-compliant; teams may join the training while withholding all data contribution.

programs.title: Governing Shared Resources: A DAO Literacy Program for Nonprofit Boards
outcomes: Distinguish agent operations from human-reserved governance decisions
Assess a contribution model against measurable outcomes
Draft board-level safeguards for AI-assisted workflows

sessions.activity: Board members study the charter structure: mission, contribution model, measurable outcomes, and the list of actions reserved for humans.
Board simulation: an AI-drafted grant proposal is reviewed; the board debates and casts a mock final vote, practicing its reserved role.
Participants critique a sample progress report against charter outcomes and write improved measurable indicators.
Boards map which of their own tasks could be delegated to agents versus which must stay with trustees, using the reserved-actions list.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized board-simulation voting patterns and rubric scores; aggregated lists of which tasks boards reserve to humans; no organization-identifying detail.
programs.consent: Board-level participation agreement; individual anonymization guaranteed; GDPR-compliant data notice; any board may participate fully without contributing data.
